items.title: Australian wrestler Bronson Reed dies aged 38, WWE says
items.summary: Tributes have flooded in for the 38-year-old Australian who is survived by his pregnant wife, Paige, their daughter.
items.body: Professional wrestler Bronson Reed has died aged 38, World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE) has announced. The company said the wrestler, whose real name is Jermaine Haley, died on Friday due to medical complications but did not give further details.

items.title: 'Poison seller' Kenneth Law apologises in court to the families of his victims
items.summary: The Canadian man, who pleaded guilty to 14 counts of aiding and abetting suicide earlier this year, said he was remorseful for his actions.
items.body: The Canadian man who sold toxic chemicals through online suicide forums in 40 countries apologised in court to the families of the victims, saying he deeply regrets his actions and will never repeat them. Kenneth Law made the remarks on Friday during a sentencing hearing where prosecutors asked a judge to give him a 25-year prison term.

items.title: Turkish officials 'destroyed' pro-opposition TV channel, owner tells BBC
items.summary: The headquarters of Halk TV were raided last month, the latest in a series of crackdowns on news sources deemed critical of the government.
items.body: Turkish authorities have "destroyed" one of the country's most-watched news channels, its London-based owner has told the BBC. Speaking to the BBC's Newshour, Cafer Mahiroğlu said that nine people connected to Halk TV were arrested this week on charges including money laundering, bribery and spreading misleading information.

items.title: Argentina fails to block oil drilling off Falkland Islands
items.summary: UK government calls on Buenos Aires to end ‘economic pressure’ on islands after international tribunal’s ruling The UK has called on Argentina to stop its economic warfare on the Falkland islands after Buenos Aires failed in a legal attempt to terminate an offshore oil project vital to the future of the British overseas territory. An application by the South American country for suspension of the Sea Lion project was rejected on Saturday by the international tribunal for the law of the seas (Itlos) on the grounds that the issue lay outside its jurisdiction.
items.body: The UK has called on Argentina to stop its economic warfare on the Falkland islands after Buenos Aires failed in a legal attempt to terminate an offshore oil project vital to the future of the British overseas territory.

items.title: ‘Who asked that? You should be ashamed of yourself!’: Judi Dench answers questions from Ian McKellen, Lorraine Kelly, David Hare and more
items.summary: Fans and famous friends put their nosiest questions to the 91-year-old actor It’s mid-afternoon and Judi Dench and I are sitting in the “den” of her country house in Surrey. It’s one of the smallest rooms in her Elizabethan home: timber beams, terracotta-painted walls, her father’s consulting-room desk and chair within touching distance, together with the bronze “Dr Dench” plaque that used to hang on the railings outside their family home in York. Behind Judi’s head hangs an enormous painting of her as M, presented as a gift on her last day of filming on Skyfall . Through the latticed windows is a view on to the garden, which is crowded with trees she plants for lost friends and family – a beloved oak, a tribute to her late husband, actor Michael Williams, towers above the pond. Even though the room is suffused with autumn sunshine, all the lights are on in the house. Judi has always needed light around her – she’s been afraid of the dark since she was small.
items.body: It’s mid-afternoon and Judi Dench and I are sitting in the “den” of her country house in Surrey.

items.title: The Fox review – talking animals are the least weird thing in this delightfully peculiar comedy
items.summary: Dario Russo’s debut feature is Brothers Grimm meets Yorgos Lanthimos, with a standout cast including Olivia Colman, Sam Neill and Emily Browning The vibe of writer-director Dario Russo’s delightfully peculiar feature debut is “messed-up fairytale”, pitched somewhere between the Brothers Grimm and Yorgos Lanthimos, with a distinctly Australian je ne sais quoi . Russo is perhaps best known for co-creating the spy comedy series Danger 5, which had an aesthetic inspired by 60s and 70s men’s magazines; The Fox has a similarly thick retro texture. I love how this film feels as though it was made in consultation with the animal world, taking place in a universe where animals can speak to humans – though that’s perhaps the least weird thing about it.
items.body: The vibe of writer-director Dario Russo’s delightfully peculiar feature debut is “messed-up fairytale”, pitched somewhere between the Brothers Grimm and Yorgos Lanthimos, with a distinctly Australian je ne sais quoi.

items.title: Astronomers ‘disheartened’ by decision allowing SpaceX to deploy satellites for space datacenters
items.summary: American Astronomical Society warned that satellites could disrupt research, while others raised concerns about orbital debris and environmental risks Astronomers are pushing back against Elon Musk’s Starmind program to place a huge number of AI computers in space, which was given the green light to proceed by federal communications regulators earlier this week. The American Astronomical Society said it was “disheartened and dismayed” by the decision by the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) decision to grant SpaceX a license to deploy as many as 1m satellites in low Earth orbit as a way of moving datacenters into space.
items.body: Astronomers are pushing back against Elon Musk’s Starmind program to place a huge number of AI computers in space, which was given the green light to proceed by federal communications regulators earlier this week.

items.title: ‘I felt a zap race through my body’: what happens when someone is hit by lightning?
items.summary: Tens of thousands of people experience strikes each year. What are the effects of a current five times hotter than the sun – and how can you keep safe? Caitlin Thomas recalls knowing that something terrible had happened but not fully understanding what. She and her partner had arrived at a music festival some 270km north of Melbourne in the early afternoon and began setting up their tents and a gazebo for shade when the sky suddenly turned dark and the rain became incredibly heavy. A huge gust of wind picked up and Thomas asked her partner to hold on to the gazebo so it wouldn’t fly away. “He then asked me to hold on to it also so he could crack open his beer.”

items.title: Three studies link glyphosate to cancer, contradicting claims of Trump EPA
items.summary: Experts say NIH research raises concerns about chemical companies’ influence on US agency’s pesticide division The US government’s top medical research agency has released three new studies linking glyphosate, the world’s most widely used pesticide and an active ingredient in Roundup, to cancer . The National Institutes of Health (NIH) findings contradict a controversial recent Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) conclusion that the weedkiller is not a carcinogen, and deals a blow to the White House, which has been closely allied with Roundup’s producer, Bayer. The NIH’s three papers could have significant political and legal fallout. The EPA is in the process of a court-ordered re-evaluation of glyphosate’s cancer risks. The NIH findings generate new pressure for the EPA to find that the substance is linked to cancer, which would subject it to a modest increase in regulations.
items.body: The US government’s top medical research agency has released three new studies linking glyphosate, the world’s most widely used pesticide and an active ingredient in Roundup, to cancer.
